text:
BOWLING GREEN, Ky. — Veterans had the opportunity to connect with local organizations offering help with housing, employment, education and other needs during a resource expo Wednesday in Bowling Green.

The Veteran Stand Down and Resource Expo was held from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at the Kentucky Career Center on Chestnut Street. The event brought together service providers and community organizations to help veterans learn about available resources.

Volunteers of America offers assistance to veterans experiencing homelessness or facing eviction, including help with rent, utility deposits and certain household items.

“We can offer and help with security deposits, utility deposits, rental assistance, certain household items,” said Marcy Yuncer, associate director for Volunteers of America’s Western Region.

Employment support was another focus of the event.

Goodwill Kentucky helps veterans with job coaching, resume reviews and connections to potential employers. The organization also works to remove barriers that may prevent people from finding employment.

Fifth Third Bank provided information about banking services and financial literacy. The bank also highlighted a personal banker opening at its location on Nashville Road.

Educational opportunities were available through Western Kentucky University and Veterans Upward Bound.

Kent Johnson, director of military student services at WKU, said the university helps veterans, active-duty service members, National Guard and reserve members, and military-connected family members access education benefits and navigate college life.

Veterans Upward Bound also helps veterans prepare for postsecondary education, including assistance with transcripts and educational resources.

Southcentral Kentucky Community and Technical College participated in the expo, offering another connection to education and career training.

The Kentucky Office of Vocational Rehabilitation also provided information about services for eligible people with disabilities, including vocational counseling, training and employment support.

The Kentucky National Guard was represented by Danielle Rice, a soldier family readiness specialist. Her role includes connecting service members, veterans and military families with resources such as financial counseling, TRICARE assistance, crisis intervention, legal resources and military identification card services.

United Way also helped connect people with local resources through its KYnect Resources program. The online directory allows people to search for assistance with needs such as rent, utilities, food and employment.

Hope Harbor, a regional sexual trauma recovery center, offers free therapeutic counseling, emergency advocacy and legal advocacy for survivors of sexual harm, including veterans and their loved ones. The organization also operates a 24-hour hotline at 270-846-1100.

The expo provided veterans with an opportunity to learn about multiple services in one location and connect with organizations that can help address their individual needs.

AF099 · Lesson 61 of 71

TRICARE Military Health Care

Table of ContentsShowHide

The three TRICARE options

Eligibility

How TRICARE Prime works

TRICARE is the military health-care program serving:

Active duty (AD) service members

National Guard and Reserve members

Retirees

Their families, survivors, and certain former spouses worldwide

As a major component of the Military Health System, TRICARE combines the health-care resources of the uniformed services with networks of civilian health-care professionals, institutions, pharmacies, and suppliers to provide high-quality health care while maintaining the capability to support military operations.

TRICARE is a regionally managed program. Your regional contractor should be your first stop for information on enrollment, covered benefits, access standards, claim filing, costs, etc.

More info: tricare.mil

The three TRICARE options

There are three options under TRICARE:

TRICARE Prime

TRICARE Select

TRICARE Reserve Select

Active duty members are automatically enrolled in Prime. Family members must decide which option is best for them.

Special note on SSN: All military benefits - including family member benefits - are accessed using the military member's SSN. Make sure all eligible family members have the sponsor's SSN readily available.

Eligibility

TRICARE Prime

Active duty service members and their families

Retired service members and their families

Activated Guard / Reserve members and their families (called or ordered to active duty for more than 30 days in a row)

Non-activated Guard / Reserve members and their families who qualify for care under the Transitional Assistance Management Program

Retired Guard / Reserve members at age 60 and their families

Survivors

Medal of Honor recipients and their families

Qualified former spouses

TRICARE Select

Active duty family members

Retired service members and their families

Family members of activated Guard / Reserve members (called or ordered to active duty for more than 30 days in a row)

Non-activated Guard / Reserve members and their families who qualify for care under the Transitional Assistance Management Program

Retired Guard / Reserve members at age 60 and their families

Survivors

Medal of Honor recipients and their families

Qualified former spouses

TRICARE Reserve Select

For members of the Selected Reserve (and their families) who meet all of the following:

Not on active duty orders

Not covered under the Transitional Assistance Management Program

Not eligible for or enrolled in the Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) program

Note: Survivor coverage is not affected by FEHB eligibility.

Note: Members in the Individual Ready Reserve - including Navy Reserve Voluntary Training Units - do NOT qualify to purchase TRICARE Reserve Select.

Involuntary separation: Certain members of the Selected Reserve covered by TRICARE Reserve Select and involuntarily separated under other than adverse conditions (a separation other than "honorable" or "general") may have access to extended TRICARE Reserve Select coverage up to 180 days. For more information, contact your service personnel department.

TRICARE Prime enrollment

Three ways to enroll:

Online via the Beneficiary Web Enrollment website.

Call your regional contractor.

Mail the enrollment form to your regional contractor.

How TRICARE Prime works

You have an assigned Primary Care Manager (PCM) who provides most of your care. The PCM:

Is a military or network provider.

Refers you to specialists for care he or she can't provide.

Works with your regional contractor for referrals / authorizations.

Accepts your copayment and files claims for you.

text:
The Defense Health Agency has finalized a bridge contract with Leidos as part of the ongoing transition of the military’s electronic health record toward direct arrangements with providers of the EHR’s underlying technologies.

Back in June, DHA first detailed its plans to shift away from the current lead systems integrator model for the MHS Genesis system and how the agency would work with Leidos to accomplish that. DHA eyed a series of extensions to Leidos part of that process, which the agency envisioned as completing in the summer of 2027.

The new bridge contract with Leidos has a $317.9 million ceiling and covers a period of performance through the end of January 2028, the Pentagon said in its Tuesday awards digest. System reintegration, software licensing and hosting services are within the scope of the new contract.

DHA said this new contract will gradually reduce in scope until the end date and is intended to help facilitate transitions to other service providers, while also aiding in the establishment of direct relationships with MHS Genesis’ solution providers.

Oracle Health provides the main health record for MHS Genesis. DHA is also looking to enter into direct contracts with Philips North America, American Well Corp. Henry Schein and Solventum Health Information Systems.

text:
A tick-borne medical condition that rewires the human immune system to reject red meat and dairy is becoming an increasing focus of force health protection across the Department of War.

Alpha-Gal Syndrome, or AGS, is an unusual, sugar-triggered allergy initiated by the bite of the Lone Star tick and poses a unique threat to military readiness. To combat this threat, the Defense Health Agency-Public Health at Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, is leveraging advanced vector surveillance, cutting-edge tick testing, and targeted nutritional strategies to protect service members and their families.

The biological catalyst

Unlike standard food allergies, which are triggered by proteins and cause near-immediate reactions, AGS is an allergic reaction to a sugar molecule called alpha-galactose, or AG, found in all nonprimate mammalian meats and byproducts.

"Most people live their lives eating meats such as beef, pork, venison, and lamb without issue," said Jessica Jones, a biologist with the DHA-PH Vector-Borne Disease Branch at APG. "When eaten, these meats are processed through the digestive system, which does not trigger allergy antibodies."

However, when a Lone Star tick bites a human, it injects saliva containing the AG sugar directly into the skin, initiating a completely different immunological pathway.

"The types of immune response at the site of the Lone Star tick bite may start the production of allergy-causing antibodies," said Jones. “This immune response takes one to four months to fully develop, meaning an individual might eat a hamburger months after a bite and suddenly experience severe symptoms.”

Also, because alpha-galactose is a sugar molecule rather than a protein, Jones explained it is only released from the digestive tract after mammalian meat has been fully digested. This results in a delayed reaction, with symptoms manifesting two to 10 hours after consumption. These symptoms range from hives, facial swelling, and respiratory distress to severe gastrointestinal cramping, diarrhea, and potentially fatal anaphylactic shock. Due to the delay, the condition is frequently misdiagnosed as irritable bowel syndrome, also known as IBS, or inflammatory bowel disease.

An expanding ecological threat

The geographic range of the Lone Star tick is expanding rapidly northward into the Midwest and Northeast, transforming regions once thought safe into emerging hotspots. A Centers for Disease Control and Prevention study recently published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report discussed blood donor surveillance testing of 3,000 donors that revealed exceptionally high alpha-gal-specific Immunoglobulin E, or IgE, antibody commonly found in states like Arkansas (31.2%) and Missouri (26.0%).

According to Robyn Nadolny, chief of the DHA-PH Vector-Borne Disease Branch, the rise in human cases directly tracks these expanding tick populations.

"First and foremost, the explosion of the white-tailed deer population is strongly linked to increases in Lone Star tick populations," said Nadolny. "White-tailed deer are a preferred host at all life stages. They have rebounded to historic highs and thrive in suburban environments, meaning Lone Star ticks are commonly encountered even in our own backyards."

Nadolny said ecological microclimates are also driving the expansion. Invasive plant species like red cedars in the Great Plains, cogongrass in the South, and Amur honeysuckle and Japanese barberry in the East increase forest-floor humidity, enabling ticks to survive longer off-host while drawing in animal vectors. Climate change further accelerates this trend.

"Warmer winters can increase tick survival through the winters and expand the seasons when ticks are out looking for hosts," said Nadolny.

Data from the MilTICK program, which allows DOW beneficiaries to submit ticks for identification and testing, highlights this dramatic shift. In 1995, when the program began, approximately 50% of submissions were Lone Star ticks. By 2025, that number surged to over 71%.

"Indiana, for example, used to submit mainly American dog ticks, but it has shifted to being dominated by Lone Star ticks in the last 10 years," said Nadolny. "We use this long-term surveillance data to alert healthcare providers in encroaching areas to be on the lookout."

Beyond AGS, the Vector-Borne Disease Branch is monitoring other emerging threats through its newly launched MilTICK SURE Path program, which conducts off-season testing on MilTICK specimens for rare pathogens. Last year, the program detected its first Heartland virus-positive Lone Star tick, submitted from Fort Knox, Kentucky.

Navigating the mission and the mess hall

For service members diagnosed with AGS, maintaining peak physical readiness requires a strict dietary overhaul, as there is currently no cure.

"The primary intervention for a service member diagnosed with AGS is consultation with a registered dietitian nutritionist to formulate an individualized plan," said Joanna Reagan, a public health nutritionist with the DHA-PH Community Health Assessment and Action Division.

"Transitioning to a pesco-pollotarian or flexitarian dietary pattern allows service members to maintain mission readiness and body composition while eliminating mammalian antigens."

Reagan emphasized that protein targets, which range from 0.8 to 1.5 grams per kilogram of body weight for active military personnel, can easily be met using poultry, seafood, eggs, dairy, and legumes. However, micronutrients like iron require strategic planning.

"The key strategy for ensuring adequate iron intake is to combine iron found in meat poultry, fish and seafood, also known as heme iron, with nonheme iron, which is found in legumes, dark greens, and fortified grains,” said Reagan. “This should be paired with vitamin C to maximize absorption."

Reagan also advised individuals with high sensitivity to avoid mammalian byproducts like gelatin (often found in pill capsules), lard, tallow, and meat-based broths, and to monitor vitamin D3 supplements, which are often derived from mammals.

Dining facilities and operational environments present significant obstacles for active duty military personnel.

"Navigating military dining facilities requires proactive screening because standard serving lines lack comprehensive ingredient labels," said Reagan.

Reagan also explained that although the military’s Go for Green® (G4G) program helps identify healthy options, it does not screen for mammalian allergens or cross-contamination.

"Service members should engage the food service manager or culinary specialist noncommissioned officer in charge to review recipe cards and request plain poultry or fish prepared with plant-based oils on clean cookware," said Reagan.

In field environments, service members must use the Combat Rations Database, or COMRAD, to evaluate operational rations. While certain Meals, Ready-to-Eat, also known as MREs, include menu numbers on modern operational rations (such as MRE 46, Menus 2, 3, 5, 11–17, 19, and 21) and contain nonmammalian entrees, Reagan notes that side items, spreads, and accessory packs must still be rigorously screened for hidden dairy, cheese spreads, and gelatin.

Prevention remains key

Because there is no medical intervention to stop or delay AGS once sensitization begins, public health officials emphasize that personal protective measures are a service member's strongest shield.

"Tick prevention is the best defense against AGS," Nadolny concluded. "Cover up, wear permethrin-treated uniforms, use repellent on exposed skin, and conduct thorough tick checks while in tick habitats and immediately upon returning."

If bitten, service members and their families are encouraged to submit the specimen to the MilTICK program. While MilTICK cannot test tick saliva for the alpha-galactose sugar, immediate species identification can help clinicians make a faster diagnostic decision if delayed allergic symptoms emerge months later.

Official military resources

MilTICK Surveillance Program: Service members, entomologists, and military medical providers can submit ticks collected from human hosts to the DHA-PH Vector-Borne Disease Branch for identification and pathogen screening. Learn how to submit a specimen and track tick activity at the MilTICK Program Portal.

DoW Insect Repellent System: The military’s standardized personal protective system combines permethrin-treated uniforms with topical repellents (like DEET or Picaridin) to protect personnel from tick, mosquito, and fly bites in operational environments.

text:
DHA is seeking commercial tools to sustain and modernize its Data Exchange Platform

The platform routes real-time data between military health systems and more than 15 partners

Phase I proposals are due by Oct. 28

The Defense Health Agency is inviting industry proposals for commercial offerings for operating, sustaining and upgrading the Data Exchange Platform, a core conduit for clinical and operational data across the Military Health System.

DHA’s Enterprise Intelligence and Data Solutions Program Management Office released Wednesday the opportunity on SAM.gov as Area of Interest No. 2 under the agency’s commercial solutions opening.

Federal health IT modernization will be a focus at the Potomac Officers Club’s 2026 Healthcare Summit on Dec. 3, where government and industry leaders will examine innovation and the future of federal care delivery. Register now!

What Is DHA’s Data Exchange Platform?

The platform underpins core functions of the MHS Information Platform, or MIP, by processing live clinical and operational data shared with over 15 outside systems and partners. It supports secure, standards-based data-sharing among DHA, the Department of Veterans Affairs and other federal health organizations to advance military readiness and patient care.

The EIDS office previously migrated two legacy data warehouses holding more than 1 petabyte of data into MIP under Operation Helios.

What Capabilities Does DHA Want from Industry?

DHA wants vendors to keep existing services stable, secure and always available as the platform shifts toward scalable, cloud-native architecture built on application programming interfaces, open standards, and artificial intelligence and machine learning readiness.

Offerings may be ready-made or adaptable through configuration, integration or modification. Responses will help DHA weigh each offering’s maturity, feasibility and commercial viability, along with potential procurement routes.

How Can Vendors Respond?

Phase I proposal submissions are due on Oct. 28, and the agency may use any award authority listed in the CSO.

Boston Consulting Group and Andrew Morgan will serve as non-government advisers during the review, bound by conflict-of-interest and nondisclosure terms.

title: NMFA Calls for Military Family Priorities in FY27 NDAA
description:
Our priorities are clear: strengthen military family health care, expand access to high-quality and affordable child care, keep military housing safe and healthy, and support military-connected youth.
Ensuring Timely Access to Care Military families deserve timely access to care and a way to speak up when waitlists are long or care is difficult to find.
Military families deserve health coverage that gives them the opportunity to build their families when they are ready.
Caring for Military Kids and Youth Finding high-quality, affordable child care remains a persistent challenge for military families.
As Congress continues its work on the FY27 NDAA, we will continue to bring the experiences of military families to policymakers and advocate for policies that strengthen their quality of life.
text:
Each year, the National Defense Authorization Act shapes defense programs and policies that affect service members and their families. The House has passed its version of the FY27 NDAA, H.R. 8800, while the Senate continues consideration of its bill, S. 4784.

On September 17, the National Military Family Association sent a letter to leaders of the Senate and House Armed Services Committees highlighting provisions that would address challenges military families face every day. Our priorities are clear: strengthen military family health care, expand access to high-quality and affordable child care, keep military housing safe and healthy, and support military-connected youth.

Ensuring Timely Access to Care

Military families deserve timely access to care and a way to speak up when waitlists are long or care is difficult to find. The Senate bill would establish a digital system that allows TRICARE beneficiaries to report problems accessing care at military medical treatment facilities or through the TRICARE network, track the status of their concerns, and receive updates on how those concerns are being addressed.

The House-passed bill also includes a provision important to expectant families. Section 758 would create a five-year pilot treating pregnancy as a Qualifying Life Event for enrollment in TRICARE Select, giving eligible beneficiaries greater flexibility to change coverage during pregnancy rather than waiting for Open Season.

Expanding TRICARE Coverage

NMFA has long advocated for a military health benefit that meets the needs of the families it serves. In our letter, we strongly supported a House provision that would provide TRICARE coverage for fertility-related care, including IVF, for eligible active-duty service members and their families.

Military families deserve health coverage that gives them the opportunity to build their families when they are ready.

The Senate bill also includes provisions expanding TRICARE coverage to include hearing aids for eligible children of military retirees enrolled in family coverage under TRICARE Select, as well as cranial orthotic devices used to treat certain infant head-shape conditions.

Caring for Military Kids and Youth

Finding high-quality, affordable child care remains a persistent challenge for military families.

NMFA supports House provisions that would create a grant program to help providers expand infant and toddler care in areas with high costs or limited access. The provisions would also include au pairs as eligible providers in the military’s in-home child care pilot.

We also support a Senate provision that would standardize how the Department of War collects and reports information on child care capacity, staffing, and waitlists across military services and installations. Better information can help leaders understand where the gaps are and respond to families’ needs.

Keeping Homes Safe and Healthy

Every military family deserves a safe and healthy place to call home, whether they live on or off base.

Too many families continue to report mold, dampness, pest infestations, and other health and safety concerns in privatized military housing. NMFA supports Senate provisions that would establish stronger health and safety standards, require independent inspections following certain tenant complaints or remediation efforts, and strengthen protections for families who report housing problems.

As Congress continues its work on the FY27 NDAA, we will continue to bring the experiences of military families to policymakers and advocate for policies that strengthen their quality of life.

text:
An Oklahoma chiropractor who owned a medical supply company was sentenced Thursday, Oct. 8, to 14 years in federal prison for a scheme that billed Medicare, TRICARE and CHAMPVA more than $30 million for braces and other equipment, the U.S. Department of Justice said. Mark Loftis, 39, of Cushing, Oklahoma, was also ordered to pay more than $8 million in restitution and forfeit more than $560,000.

The scheme relied on equipment orders signed by telemedicine doctors and nurse practitioners who never examined the patients and often never spoke with them, according to prosecutors. Many of the people listed on those orders were older adults and people with disabilities who did not want or need the equipment.

The case matters well beyond Oklahoma. Every older adult, veteran, or military family member with federal coverage is a potential target of the same playbook. Unneeded orders billed in a person's name can also make it harder to get coverage for equipment they truly need later, according to federal investigators.

The Mechanics of a Sham Telemedicine Order

A federal jury in the Middle District of Florida convicted Loftis on July 21 of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud after a 12-day trial, the DOJ said in its conviction announcement. His company, Back Pain Home Supplies, which did business as EZ Medical Supply, was based in Drumright, Oklahoma. Assistant Deputy Chief Catherine Wagner and Trial Attorney Raymond Beckering III of the Justice Department's Health Care Fraud Section tried the case.

Prosecutors said Loftis paid more than $1 million in illegal kickbacks, including through a shell marketing company, to marketers, purported telemedicine companies and a call center. Those marketers persuaded older and disabled people to share personal and insurance information and accept equipment such as orthotic braces and continuous glucose monitors.

The co-conspirators then bought signed orders for that equipment from telemedicine clinicians who had no real relationship with the patients. In one example cited by prosecutors, eight braces were billed for a single beneficiary at once. Of the more than $30 million billed, programs paid about $8 million.

Loftis also hid from Medicare who truly owned and managed the company, and that other unenrolled suppliers were billing through it, according to the DOJ. He kept the scheme going for about three years despite steady complaints from beneficiaries and relatives, including families of parents living with dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

"The defendant turned private medical data into a pipeline for personal profit," Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division said after the verdict.

Harm to Patients Goes Beyond Taxpayer Dollars

Fraud like this is not victimless for the patients whose names are used. The HHS Office of Inspector General warns that if unneeded braces are billed to Medicare, "Medicare may deny a brace that the beneficiary needs in the future."

Federal auditors have flagged braces as a weak spot for years. A 2024 OIG review found Medicare paid about $5.3 billion for orthotic braces from 2014 through 2020. It identified orders from providers with no treating relationship and suppliers using banned solicitation, and warned of potential harm to enrollees.

Those most at risk include older adults living alone, people with memory loss, veterans enrolled in CHAMPVA and military families on TRICARE. Caregivers who manage a parent's mail and benefits are often the first to spot unexpected boxes or unfamiliar charges.

"Healthcare fraud drains millions of dollars from federally funded programs, and we all pay the price," said Rodney Crawford, special agent in charge of the FBI's Tampa field office. The case was investigated by HHS-OIG, the FBI, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service and the VA Office of Inspector General.

The restitution order of more than $8 million roughly matches what the programs actually paid on the false claims, money that came from the same federal funds that cover care for older adults, service members and veterans.

Legitimate Telehealth and the Warning Signs of a Scam

None of this means telehealth itself is unsafe. Many patients use video and phone visits with their own clinicians to manage chronic conditions, refill prescriptions, and avoid long drives. The problem in this case was the use of telemedicine as a cover for orders that no real clinician-patient relationship supported.

Federal investigators list clear red flags. These include an unsolicited call or ad offering a free brace covered by Medicare, equipment arriving without a doctor's order, and anyone other than your own doctor's office asking for your Medicare number. A real telehealth visit is usually one you scheduled, with a clinician who reviews your history and explains why equipment is needed.

Beneficiaries and caregivers can take a few simple steps. Hang up on unsolicited equipment offers and never share a Medicare, TRICARE, or VA number with callers. Refuse or return any item your own doctor did not order, and note the sender's name and the date. Review Medicare statements or plan summaries for items you never received.

Suspected fraud can be reported to the HHS OIG hotline at 1-800-447-8477 or online at tips.hhs.gov. Anyone who believes their medical identity was misused should also ask their doctor to review their records for errors.

The DOJ has not announced charges against the individual clinicians who signed the orders in this case. MedicalDaily will update this story if prosecutors release more information about co-conspirators or any appeal.

Key Questions Answered

Who was sentenced, and for what?

Mark Loftis, 39, of Cushing, Oklahoma, was sentenced to 14 years in prison for conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud tied to more than $30 million in false claims.

How did the telemedicine part of the scheme work?

Prosecutors said co-conspirators bought equipment orders signed by telemedicine doctors and nurse practitioners who never examined the patients and often never spoke with them.

Which programs were billed?

Medicare, TRICARE and CHAMPVA were billed for orthotic braces, continuous glucose monitors and other equipment.

Can fraud billed in my name affect my coverage?

Yes. HHS-OIG warns that if unneeded braces are billed to Medicare, Medicare may deny a brace you actually need later.

What are signs of a brace or equipment scam?

Unsolicited calls offering free braces, equipment arriving without a doctor's order, and strangers asking for your Medicare number are common warning signs.

What should I do if I receive equipment I did not order?

Refuse or return it, record the sender and date, and report it to the HHS OIG hotline at 1-800-447-8477 or tips.hhs.gov.

Is telehealth unsafe to use?

No. Legitimate telehealth with your own clinicians is widely used and safe. The concern is orders from clinicians who have no real relationship with the patient.

text:
Democrat U.S. Rep. Vicente Gonzalez is claiming in a new campaign ad that he has never supported sex-change procedures for children, despite previously voting against legislation aimed at restricting the treatments.

In the ad, Gonzalez pushes back against criticism of his record, declaring, “I’ve never supported sex changes for kids.”

But his voting record tells a different story.

Gonzalez has repeatedly cosponsored the Equality Act, which he supported in four consecutive Congresses.

The legislation would expand federal nondiscrimination protections based on sexual orientation and gender identity. Critics argue it could be used to challenge restrictions on gender mutilation procedures.

Gonzalez also voted against amendments to defense legislation in 2023 that sought to restrict military healthcare programs from covering or providing certain gender-transition procedures.

One amendment would have prohibited TRICARE from covering sex-change surgeries and hormone treatments. Another targeted gender-transition procedures through the military’s Exceptional Family Member Program, including treatments for dependent children.

Last year, Gonzalez voted against the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which included a provision restricting Medicaid funding for gender-transition procedures.

“Out of touch Vicente Gonzalez is a gutless hypocrite who lectures parents about protecting children while he voted to greenlight puberty blockers, cross-sex hormones, and irreversible surgeries on minors,” said NRCC spokesman Christian Martinez.

“He can’t explain his own radical record because he knows it’s sick.”

Gonzalez also takes aim at his Republican challenger, Eric Flores, in the ad.

“Eric Flores stands with abusers. I stand with the survivors,” Gonzalez says.

However, Gonzalez’ own legal career included representing a defendant accused of assaulting his pregnant girlfriend.

According to a 2000 court case cited by Republicans, Gonzalez represented Luis Ramirez Martinez, who was accused of repeatedly punching his girlfriend after learning she was pregnant, causing her to fall to the ground.

Martinez pleaded guilty to assault causing bodily injury and received 180 days of community supervision following a plea agreement.

The case adds to scrutiny of Gonzalez’ legal career, which Republicans have previously highlighted in attacks over his representation of defendants charged with drug trafficking and human smuggling.
